brief: Goldman's weekly positioning wrap (Positioning Mondays, week of 12 Oct) tracks several desks. Fundamental long/short funds raised gross leverage (+3.3pts to 209.5%) but cut net leverage further (-0.2pts to 52.9%, 6th percentile): rising engagement, still a bearish net stance, uncomfortable with indices near record highs. The global HF book was net sold overall (-0.3 SDs); US Info Tech flipped from the most-bought US sector in 4 of the prior 5 weeks to by far the most-sold this week after OpenAI revenue headlines drove Semi/Tech selling, which the desk reads as a sign positioning there was fuller than thought. Europe bucked the trend with a 3rd straight week of risk-on buying. The desk says Asset Managers were small net sellers on the week, while separate CFTC data shows institutions were small net buyers of S&P futures for the week ending Sept 29 (different source, different week). CTAs sold $23bn and are modeled to keep selling short-term but turn buyers over a one-month horizon. Buybacks stayed light in pre-earnings blackout while IPO supply continued. Retail, AAII, GS SI and Fear & Greed sentiment all turned more neutral or less negative; the desk sees no shortage of marginal buyers if oil/rate overhangs recede.
